subject.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): remove shell:true from Azure CLI invocations

question: Which Windows Azure CLI execution strategy should Microsoft Foundry accept before this security-sensitive PR can merge?
rationale: The current patch removes shell parsing but directly executes `az.cmd`, which conflicts with Node's Windows process contract; choosing the permanent safe launcher may require security-boundary judgment.

options.title: Require a proven shell-free launcher
options.body: Resolve Azure CLI to a real executable or safe entrypoint, cover the resolver in tests, and require Windows proof before merge.

options.title: Accept a reviewed shell fallback
options.body: Keep Windows `cmd.exe` execution only if maintainers explicitly accept the boundary and the PR adds strict validation or escaping for every user-controlled argument.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Hold or close this branch until a Windows-tested mitigation is available, because the current shape would break the target platform.

recommendation.title: Require a proven shell-free launcher
recommendation.body: Resolve Azure CLI to a real executable or safe entrypoint, cover the resolver in tests, and require Windows proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Foundry CLI refactors and maintainer-side proof/review history make this the best available routing owner for the security-boundary choice.
